hardFacts.flightFromDelhi: New Delhi to Bangkok Suvarnabhumi (BKK): 4 hours direct. Thai Airways, IndiGo, Air India, AirAsia. Return fare: INR 18,000–35,000. Book 6–8 weeks ahead.
hardFacts.flightFromMumbai: Mumbai to Bangkok: 4.5 hours direct. Multiple airlines.
hardFacts.twoAirports: BKK Suvarnabhumi (main international, closer to city). DMK Don Mueang (budget airlines — AirAsia, Nok Air). They are 30km apart. Check which airport carefully.
hardFacts.timezone: ICT (UTC+7). India is UTC+5:30. Bangkok is 1.5 hours ahead of India.
hardFacts.currency: Thai Baht (THB). THB 1 = approximately INR 2.3. USD 1 = THB 34–36. Best exchange: Superrich Thailand or Vasu exchange offices in the city — NEVER at the airport. Airport rate is 8–12% worse.
hardFacts.visaIndia: Thai tourist visa required for Indians. Best option: e-Visa at thaievisa.go.th — USD 35, 3–5 working days, 60 days single entry. Visa on Arrival available at airport (USD 35, 30 days) but queues often 2+ hours. ALWAYS apply e-Visa online before travel.
hardFacts.temperature: 28–35°C year-round with high humidity. Cool season November–February: the best months (28–32°C, less humid). Hot season March–May: 32–38°C, most uncomfortable. Rainy season June–October: heavy afternoon rain, mornings usually clear.
hardFacts.criticalRule: Bangkok traffic is legendary and unpredictable. The BTS Skytrain and MRT subway are ALWAYS faster than taxis during rush hours 7–9am and 5–8pm. A Skytrain journey that takes 12 minutes takes 45 minutes by taxi. Budget 45–90 minutes for any cross-city taxi journey in peak hours.
hardFacts.electricity: Type A and B plugs (American-style). 220V. Indian plugs need adapter. Adapters available at any 7-Eleven for THB 80–150.
hardFacts.water: Never drink tap water. Bottled water THB 10–20 for 1.5L at 7-Eleven. Always carry a bottle outdoors.

emergencyContacts.touristPolice: 1155 (English-speaking, 24/7 — the correct first call for tourists)
emergencyContacts.pharmacy24hr: Boots Pharmacy at most BTS stations, Watsons at major malls — most open until 10pm. Some 24-hour at major hospitals.

policeStations.name: Tourist Police Division HQ
policeStations.address: Unico House, Lumphini area — handles all tourist complaints

policeStations.name: Phra Nakhon Police Station
policeStations.area: Old City, Rattanakosin, Khao San Road

firstVisitorEssentials.summary: First-time Bangkok visitor. The temples are genuine and extraordinary — see them before 10am. The street food is the finest in Southeast Asia. The city rewards patience and slowing down.
mustInclude: Wat Pho at 8am — Temple of the Reclining Buddha, 46-metre gold Buddha, arrive before tour groups, THB 200
Grand Palace — THB 500, morning only, dress code strictly enforced (shoulders and knees covered), most photographed site in Thailand
Chao Phraya River orange-flag express boat — THB 15/stop, not the tourist boat, the workers' boat
Chatuchak Weekend Market — Saturday–Sunday only, 8,000 stalls, arrive 9am before heat, Mo Chit BTS
Yaowarat (Chinatown) street food at night — from 7pm, walk the main road and every side alley
firstVisitorEssentials.localInsiderToAdd: Most visitors stay near Khao San Road or Sukhumvit and eat pad thai every meal. The Bangkok that matters starts one street behind the tourist strip — the locals who have lived here 20 years eat in places with no English menu and the food is dramatically better.
regrets: Took a tuk-tuk when driver offered a temple tour — all tuk-tuk tour offers lead to gem shops or tailors earning commission. Use Grab for all transport.
Didn't eat from street stalls — Bangkok street food is statistically safer than most restaurant kitchens due to turnover. The stall with 30 locals queuing is the correct choice.
Visited temples in the afternoon — all temples better before 10am: cooler, quieter, better light, genuine worshippers
Stayed entirely on Khao San Road — it is the tourist bubble. The city starts one street away.
Skipped the river — Chao Phraya express boat for THB 15 gives the best Bangkok perspective available

repeatVisitorIntelligence.insiderNarrative: The Bangkok most visitors see was built for visitors. Fifteen minutes from Khao San Road in any direction is a city that has never heard of pad thai as a tourist dish.
skipThese: Khao San Road as primary base
Floating market by tourist bus — the local markets are better and cheaper
goHere: Bang Krachao — the green lung of Bangkok. Ferry from Klong Toei pier THB 4, bicycle hire THB 50/day, mangrove forest, no cars, almost no tourists
Talad Noi — oldest Chinese neighbourhood, Portuguese shophouses, quiet lanes, excellent local coffee shops run by artists
Or Tor Kor Market — where Bangkok's chefs shop, finest fresh produce, prepared food section beats any restaurant
Ari neighbourhood — where young Bangkok professionals live, independent cafés, creative food, zero tourists
Damnoen Saduak floating market at 5:30am — before tour boats arrive, completely different experience
Jim Thompson House — Thai silk heritage, beautiful gardens, consistently overlooked by tourists
Nang Loeng Market — Bangkok's oldest market, 1900s architecture, incredible traditional Thai food, locals only

old_city_rattanakosin.character: The historical heart. Grand Palace, Wat Pho, Wat Arun, National Museum. The tourist circuit here is entirely justified — these are genuinely extraordinary monuments. But see them at dawn, not noon.
avoid: Afternoon visits — heat and crowd ruin the experience
Tuk-tuk tours offered outside temple entrances — commission shops
old_city_rattanakosin.insider: Wat Pho at 8am when monks are chanting and incense is fresh — this is a working temple, not a tourist attraction. The traditional Thai massage school inside Wat Pho charges THB 260/hour for one of the best massage experiences in Bangkok.

sukhumvit.character: Bangkok's expat and upscale tourist corridor. BTS-connected, full of malls, excellent international dining and nightlife. The most convenient base but most removed from real Bangkok.
avoid: Nana Plaza area if not interested in red-light district
Overpriced tourist restaurants on the main Sukhumvit strip when identical food exists on side sois
sukhumvit.insider: The quiet-numbered sois (side streets) off Sukhumvit — Soi 38 (local food market), Soi 49 (residential dining) — have excellent restaurants at a fraction of main strip prices.

silom.character: Bangkok's financial district. More local than Sukhumvit, excellent Indian food at Bangrak area, Patpong Night Market, Lumphini Park adjacent.
silom.insider: Silom Soi 20 has a concentration of excellent local restaurants serving southern Thai food — the most complex and spicy regional Thai cuisine, completely absent from tourist menus.

chinatown_yaowarat.character: The most visually spectacular neighbourhood in Bangkok. Neon signs, smoke from street grills, gold shops, herbalists, and the city's best street seafood. Come at night.
avoid: Visiting before 5pm — the market comes alive at night
chinatown_yaowarat.insider: The oyster omelette stalls that appear on side streets after 7pm. This dish is specific to Yaowarat and unlike any oyster preparation elsewhere in Bangkok. Walk every side alley off the main road.

bang_krachao.character: A peninsula in a bend of the Chao Phraya technically part of Bangkok but feels like rural Thailand from the 1970s. Bicycle paths through mangrove forest, wooden houses on stilts, weekend floating market. The air is noticeably different.
bestFor: Escape from city — full sensory contrast
avoid: Visiting without a bicycle — walking the paths is inefficient
bang_krachao.insider: Ferry from Klong Toei pier costs THB 4 and takes 10 minutes. The island has been protected by its location in the river bend from development since the 1960s. The Sri Nakhon Khuean Khan Park and Botanical Garden is free to enter.

thonglor_ekkamai.character: The trendiest neighbourhood in Bangkok. Japanese expat community, best cocktail bars in the city, independent coffee culture, farm-to-table restaurants. Where Bangkok's wealthy young professionals go on weekends.
thonglor_ekkamai.insider: Thonglor soi 17 has a concentration of Japanese restaurants run by actual Japanese chefs — the Japanese expat community is so large here that standards are genuinely comparable to Tokyo.

ari.character: The neighbourhood where young creative professionals live. Independent coffee roasters, vinyl record shops, art galleries, food trucks. Zero tourists. 15 minutes from the tourist corridor.
ari.insider: Ari BTS station area on a Sunday morning. The weekend market behind the station has Bangkok's best artisanal food producers. The roasted duck stall that opens at 7am has been operating since the 1950s.

restaurants.name: Jay Fai
restaurants.orderThis: Crab omelette THB 1,000, Drunken noodles THB 400
restaurants.insider: A 70-year-old woman in ski goggles against the wok flames has been cooking here since the 1980s and now has a Michelin star. The crab omelette is the most-ordered dish in Bangkok by people who know what they are eating. The queue is real. The 2 hours are worth it.

restaurants.name: Or Tor Kor Market Food Court
restaurants.orderThis: Mango sticky rice THB 60, Grilled pork THB 80, Som tum THB 50, Anything from any stall
restaurants.insider: Bangkok's professional chefs shop here for ingredients. Air-conditioned, clean, and the prepared food section contains dishes that don't appear on any restaurant menu. The mango sticky rice uses mangoes at peak ripeness because vendors compete with each other daily.

restaurants.name: Gaggan Anand
restaurants.orderThis: Tasting menu only — THB 6,500/person. Menu arrives as emojis.
restaurants.insider: The best Indian food outside India is in Bangkok. Chef Gaggan Anand reimagines Indian cuisine with molecular gastronomy. The emoji menu is not a gimmick — it is the dish list. Every Indian traveller who visits should eat here once. Nothing else in the world tastes like this.

restaurants.name: Somtum Der
restaurants.orderThis: Som tum papaya salad THB 90, Larb moo THB 120, Sticky rice THB 30
restaurants.insider: Isaan food is what Thai people actually eat at home. Not on tourist menus. The fermented fish version of som tum is what it actually tastes like. Order it. The version without fermented fish is the tourist version.

restaurants.name: Yaowarat Street Food — Oyster Omelette
restaurants.orderThis: Oyster omelette THB 100, Grilled seafood cart THB 80–200, Braised pork leg rice THB 80
restaurants.insider: Yaowarat at 8pm on a weekend: vendors, smoke, neon, families, tourists all compressed into one street. Walk slowly. Eat from stalls with the longest local queues. The oyster omelette is specific to this street and unlike any oyster dish you have had anywhere.

restaurants.name: Nahm
restaurants.insider: Chef David Thompson spent 20 years researching Thai royal court cuisine. The recipes are from 19th-century manuscripts. This is not the Thai food you have eaten before — it is the version that existed before the international palette softened everything.

restaurants.name: Bo.lan
restaurants.insider: The most sustainable restaurant in Bangkok. Every ingredient sourced from small Thai farms. The menu changes with the season and never repeats. The couple who run this restaurant trained at Nahm and opened their own vision of Thai food in a heritage house garden.

restaurants.name: Nang Loeng Market
restaurants.orderThis: Pad see ew THB 60, Khao man gai THB 55, Mango sticky rice THB 50
restaurants.insider: Bangkok's oldest surviving market, built in 1899. Art Deco shophouses around a covered market. The Thai desserts here are made by the same families who have been making them for three generations. Almost no tourists. The food is extraordinary and costs THB 30–80 per item.

restaurants.name: Raan Jay Fai (neighbourhood equivalent)
restaurants.orderThis: Pad kra pao (basil stir fry) THB 80, Tom yum THB 120
restaurants.insider: The neighbourhood home cooking restaurants on the side streets of Banglamphu. No English menu, no tourist positioning, the same food as Jay Fai at one-tenth the price. Ask hotel staff in the area where they eat.

restaurants.name: Supanniga Eating Room
restaurants.orderThis: Crying tiger beef THB 380, Supanniga shrimp paste rice THB 280, Mango salad THB 220
restaurants.insider: A restaurant serving the home cooking of Chanthaburi province in eastern Thailand — a region known for some of the finest fruit and seafood in the country. The recipes came from the owner's grandmother. This food exists nowhere in the tourist circuit.

restaurants.name: Thip Samai (Pad Thai)
restaurants.orderThis: Pad Thai wrapped in egg THB 120, Prawn pad Thai THB 140
restaurants.insider: Open since 1966. The pad Thai here is wrapped in a thin egg omelette. This is the dish — not the tourist pad Thai served everywhere else in Bangkok. The orange juice squeezed to order alongside it is the correct accompaniment. Queue is 20–40 minutes but moves fast.

restaurants.name: Breakfast at Prempracha's Kitchen
restaurants.orderThis: Jok (rice porridge) THB 50, Kai jeow (Thai omelette on rice) THB 60, Patongo (deep fried dough) THB 20
restaurants.insider: The Thai breakfast that Bangkok's office workers eat every day. Jok rice porridge with pork and egg, fresh patongo dough sticks, strong Thai iced coffee. The version of Bangkok breakfast that exists before any tourist wakes up.

restaurants.name: Vertigo and Moon Bar — Banyan Tree Hotel
restaurants.pricePerPerson: THB 600–4,000 depending on dinner vs drinks
restaurants.insider: 61st floor open-air rooftop. The 360° Bangkok skyline view at sunset. Book the first seating at 5:30pm for the transition from day to night. The bar alone (no dinner) offers the same view at drinks prices.

restaurants.name: Paste Restaurant
restaurants.insider: Chef Bee Satongun won the Asia's Best Female Chef award. The food is classical Thai royal cuisine reimagined with modern technique. The curry pastes are all made in-house from fresh ingredients — something no other luxury Thai restaurant does consistently.

restaurants.name: Polo Fried Chicken
restaurants.orderThis: Fried chicken leg THB 80, Sticky rice THB 15, Papaya salad THB 60
restaurants.insider: Bangkok's most famous fried chicken restaurant, open since 1974. The chicken is marinated in garlic and coriander root, fried crispy outside and moist inside. The Bangkok diplomatic community has been eating here for 50 years. Prime location next to the US Embassy means it's surrounded by expats and locals, never tourists.

activities.name: Wat Pho — Temple of Reclining Buddha
activities.insider: The 46-metre reclining Buddha fills an entire building. You walk around it in a circle. Most visitors look at the feet and leave. Stay longer — the ceiling, the mother-of-pearl inlay on the feet, the 108 bronze bowls. The temple also contains one of Bangkok's oldest traditional massage schools (THB 260/hour).

activities.name: Chao Phraya Orange-Flag Express Boat
activities.bestTime: Morning 7–9am or evening 4–6pm for light and authentic commuter experience
activities.book: No booking. Buy ticket at pier.
activities.insider: The orange-flag boat is the workers' boat — stops at every pier, packed with commuters, completely authentic. The tourist boat (THB 40 unlimited) visits the same places. Take the orange-flag boat for one journey in each direction. THB 15 is the cheapest and most honest view of Bangkok.

activities.name: Bang Krachao Bicycle Day
activities.bestTime: 8am–noon before heat. Weekend for floating market.
activities.book: No booking. Ferry departs when sufficient passengers.
activities.insider: A peninsula in a bend of the Chao Phraya that feels like rural Thailand from the 1970s. Bicycle paths through mangrove forest, wooden houses on stilts, almost no tourists. The air is noticeably different from the city fifteen minutes away by ferry. The Sri Nakhon Khuean Khan Park has the best picnic area in Bangkok.

activities.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
activities.price: Free entry. Budget THB 500–2,000 for shopping.
activities.bestTime: Saturday or Sunday 9am–noon. After noon: very hot and crowded.
activities.insider: 8,000 stalls across 35 acres. Section 2–3 has vintage and antiques. Section 7 has plants. Section 26 has art. The food section in the interior is better than most restaurants. The map available at the entrance is essential — without it you see 2% of the market.

activities.name: Muay Thai at Rajadamnern Stadium
activities.book: Book ringside at stadium box office or online.
activities.insider: Rajadamnern is the oldest Muay Thai stadium in Thailand (1945). The ringside experience — the smell of liniment, the crowd gambling, the monks blessing fighters — is unlike any sporting event you have attended. Lumphini Stadium (Tuesday, Friday) is the newer venue but Rajadamnern has more history.

activities.name: Thai Cooking Class
activities.area: Various — Blue Elephant (luxury), Helping Hands (social enterprise)
activities.insider: The class starts at the morning market where you shop for ingredients. You learn that Thai cooking uses 11 specific base ingredients (base genep equivalent) in almost every dish — understanding this foundation changes how you taste Thai food for the rest of your life.

activities.name: Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew
activities.bestTime: Opening 8:30am. Dress code: shoulders covered, knees covered, no flip flops.
activities.book: Walk-in. Hire official guide inside (THB 200–400) not touts outside.
activities.insider: The most visited site in Thailand. Emerald Buddha (Wat Phra Kaew) is 75cm tall — smaller than expected, housed in the most ornate temple you will see anywhere. The Grand Palace grounds are extraordinary. Come at opening — by 10am tour groups dominate every major viewpoint.

activities.name: Wat Arun — Temple of Dawn
activities.area: Thonburi side of Chao Phraya, opposite Grand Palace
activities.bestTime: Sunrise 6am for photographers. Late afternoon 4pm for fewer crowds.
activities.book: Walk-in. Cross river by ferry THB 4 from Maharaj pier.
activities.insider: The most photographed temple in Bangkok from the river. Up close: the tower is covered in fragments of Chinese porcelain — ships brought porcelain as ballast, and when broken, it was used for temple decoration. The detail is extraordinary and invisible in photographs.

activities.name: Jim Thompson House
activities.insider: An American silk entrepreneur who revived the Thai silk industry disappeared in Malaysia in 1967. His house — six traditional Thai houses merged into one — remains exactly as he left it, with his extraordinary art collection. One of the best house museums in Southeast Asia and consistently overlooked by tourists who don't know who Jim Thompson was.

activities.name: Lumphini Park Morning
activities.insider: Bangkok's central park at dawn has outdoor aerobics classes, tai chi groups, people releasing turtles into the lake, and massive monitor lizards (up to 1.5m) walking across the paths completely unconcerned by humans. Free. The monitor lizards are genuinely extraordinary — they are not caged, they simply live here.

activities.name: Khlong Lat Mayom Floating Market
activities.area: Taling Chan district (40 mins from city)
activities.insider: The floating market Bangkok residents actually go to — not the tourist version at Damnoen Saduak. Fresh produce sellers on boats, cooked food on the banks, canal atmosphere without tour buses. The mango with chilli salt here is the finest version of this dish in Bangkok.

activities.name: Talad Rot Fai Night Market (Train Market)
activities.area: Ratchada area, near Thailand Cultural Centre MRT
activities.insider: A hipster vintage market with food vendors, bar stalls, and collectors' items. Thai youth culture on display — fashion, music, food, vintage cars. The green neon lights and the density of activity make it one of the best photography environments in Bangkok.

activities.name: National Museum Bangkok
activities.area: Na Phra That Road, Old City
activities.bestTime: Morning weekday. Free guided tours in English: Wed and Thu 9:30am.
activities.insider: The most important collection of Thai art and history in the world. The Buddha collection — spanning 2,000 years — puts every temple visit in context. Completely undervisited. The Wednesday/Thursday English free guided tour by volunteer guides is one of the finest cultural experiences available in Bangkok.

activities.name: Rooftop Sunset at Above Eleven
activities.price: THB 300–500 cocktails. No minimum at bar.
activities.book: Walk-in for bar seating. aboveeleven.com for table reservation.
activities.insider: 33-floor rooftop bar with the best view of the Sukhumvit skyline. The Peruvian-Japanese cocktail menu is surprisingly excellent. More accessible and less pretentious than the famous Sky Bar at Lebua. The correct Bangkok rooftop bar for most travellers.

solo.experience: Bang Krachao at 8am on a weekday
solo.details: Ferry from Klong Toei pier (THB 4), hire bicycle (THB 50), ride through mangrove forest and stilted villages. No cars. No tourists. The air is genuinely different from the city fifteen minutes away.
solo.why: Solo travellers who find this place describe it as the moment Bangkok stopped being a tourist destination and started being somewhere real.

couple.details: Oldest Chinese neighbourhood in Bangkok. Portuguese shophouses from the 1800s. Cats sleeping on motorcycles. Coffee shops in converted warehouses run by art students. The neighbourhood that hasn't been discovered yet.
couple.why: Couples who walk Talad Noi together have something to talk about at dinner that no other tourist does.

foodie.details: Bangkok's professional chefs shop here. The durian is the finest in the country, cut to order. The mango sticky rice uses glutinous rice soaked overnight. The prepared food has dishes that don't appear on any restaurant menu.
foodie.why: Every food-focused traveller who finds Or Tor Kor describes it as the best food hour of the entire trip.

budget.experience: THB 15 orange-flag boat ride at sunset
budget.details: Buy a ticket at any Chao Phraya pier. Board the crowded orange-flag boat. Ride 8 stops at golden hour. Watch the city from the water — temples, markets, office buildings, houses on stilts. THB 15.
budget.why: The best view of Bangkok costs THB 15. Most tourists pay THB 800 for a tourist cruise of the same river.

photographer.details: Before the evening vendors arrive, Chinatown at dawn is a working neighbourhood — elderly men playing chess, temple smoke, produce deliveries, golden light on red shop fronts. The neon signs visible in a completely different context at dawn.
photographer.why: The Yaowarat photograph nobody else has is the 7am version, not the 9pm version.

honeymoon.experience: Private longtail boat along the canals at sunset
honeymoon.details: Charter a private longtail boat from any riverside pier (THB 1,500–2,000/hour). Ask the driver to take the small khlongs — not the river. The canals behind the city have temples, gardens, and houses that look exactly as they did fifty years ago.
honeymoon.why: The canals at sunset are Bangkok without the traffic — which is the Bangkok worth seeing.

family.experience: Lumphini Park at 6:30am for monitor lizards
family.details: Bangkok's central park at dawn has massive monitor lizards (1–1.5m) walking across paths completely unconcerned by humans. Outdoor aerobics, tai chi groups, turtle releases. Free. Children who see their first monitor lizard in the wild talk about it for years.
family.why: The monitor lizards at Lumphini are the most unexpected family experience in Bangkok.

adventure.experience: Muay Thai evening at Rajadamnern Stadium
adventure.details: Ringside seats THB 2,000–3,000. The oldest stadium in Thailand (1945). Monks bless fighters. The crowd gambles using hand signals. The physical intensity of watching professionals fight at close range.
adventure.why: Every adventure traveller who attends Muay Thai at Rajadamnern describes it as one of the most intense evenings they have had anywhere.

luxury.details: The restaurant menu arrives as emojis. What you eat over three hours is unlike any meal anywhere. Asia's Best Restaurant. THB 6,500/person. Every Indian traveller should eat here once in their life.
luxury.why: Every Indian who eats at Gaggan describes it as the best meal of their life.

solo.accommodation: Lub d Silom or Lub d Siam — best social hostels in Bangkok. Air-conditioned common areas, pool, events. THB 400–800 dorm, THB 1,500–2,500 private.
solo.meetingPeople: Free walking tours (Bangkok Free Tours), cooking classes, Muay Thai evenings, rooftop bars in Sukhumvit
solo.safety: Bangkok is safe for solo travellers. Main risk: tuk-tuk commission scams. Use Grab for all transport. Tourist Police on 1155.
solo.itineraryLogic: Solo travellers can cover Wat Pho, Chao Phraya, and Chinatown in one efficient day. Second day: neighbourhood exploration in Bang Krachao or Ari.

couple.bestExperiences: Private longtail canal tour at sunset, cooking class together, Muay Thai evening, rooftop dinner at Vertigo
couple.bestNeighbourhood: Thonglor for dining. Silom for bars. Old City for history.
couple.avoid: Khao San Road for a couples trip — not the atmosphere

honeymoon.accommodation: Capella Bangkok, Mandarin Oriental (opened 1876), Peninsula Bangkok. THB 8,000–25,000/night.
honeymoon.experiences: Private chef boat dinner on the Chao Phraya, Gaggan Anand dinner, Jim Thompson House private tour, Spa at the Oriental
honeymoon.insider: The Mandarin Oriental Bangkok opened in 1876 and has hosted every significant writer, diplomat, and monarch who visited Bangkok. The Authors' Lounge for afternoon tea is the most historic room in Thailand's hospitality.

family.bestActivities: Chatuchak Weekend Market (kids love it), cooking class family version, Khlong Lat Mayom floating market, Lumphini Park monitor lizards
family.accommodation: Sukhumvit soi 11–19 area — best malls, parks, BTS access, international restaurants
family.heatManagement: Bangkok heat with children: AC activities 11am–4pm. Temple visits before 10am only.

budget.accommodation: Hostels in Banglamphu or Silom: THB 300–600 dorm, THB 800–1,200 private
budget.foodStrategy: Street food all three meals. THB 40–120 per dish. 7-Eleven for breakfast — genuinely good onigiri and hot foods.
budget.freeActivities: All wat grounds free to walk. Lumphini Park. Bang Krachao (only ferry + bicycle cost THB 54). Chatuchak entry free.

senior.accommodation: Silom or Riverside hotels — lower floors, BTS accessible, no need for tuk-tuks or scooters
senior.heatManagement: Plan all outdoor activities before 10am. Afternoon: malls, museums, hotel pool. The National Museum free tour Wed/Thu 9:30am is ideal — air-conditioned, guided, genuine content.
senior.bestActivities: Chao Phraya boat (seated, breezy), National Museum English tour, Thai massage at Wat Pho school, Jim Thompson House

photographer.goldenHour: 6:30–8am (Wat Arun at sunrise from the river). 5:30–7pm (Yaowarat neon at dusk, rooftop views).
photographer.locations: Wat Arun from river at dawn, Yaowarat at rain on a Friday night, Wat Pho interior at 8am, Or Tor Kor sellers at 8am, Bang Krachao canal reflections
photographer.equipment: Rainy season: sealed bags essential. Humidity causes sensor dust faster than dry climates.

indian.indianFood: Bangrak area near Silom: excellent Indian restaurants — Rang Mahal, Indus, Taj Indian Restaurant. Authentic South and North Indian at proper prices.
indian.temples: Sri Maha Mariamman Temple (Indian Temple, Silom) — the most important Hindu temple in Bangkok, built by Tamil traders in the 1800s
indian.community: Bangkok has a significant Indian trading community in the Pahurat area (Little India) near the Old City — textiles, gold, Indian food at Indian prices

luxury.name: Mandarin Oriental Bangkok
luxury.honest: Opened 1876. The most historic hotel in Southeast Asia. The Authors' Lounge has had more significant guests than any room in Asia. The spa is the finest in Bangkok.
luxury.tip: The Garden Wing is more beautiful than the River Wing and cheaper.

luxury.name: Capella Bangkok
luxury.honest: The most visually spectacular hotel in Bangkok. Every room faces the Chao Phraya. Only opened 2020.

mid.name: 137 Pillars Suites Bangkok
mid.honest: All-suite hotel in a converted heritage building. Best value luxury in Bangkok.

mid.name: Hotel Muse Bangkok
mid.honest: Boutique luxury at mid-range prices. Art-themed rooms. Great location.

budget.name: Lub d Silom
budget.honest: Best social hostel in Bangkok. Pool, rooftop, events programme.

budget.name: Onederz Hostel
budget.honest: Clean, well-located, social. Best base for Old City exploration.

transport.bts_skytrain: BTS Sukhumvit Line (eastern Bangkok) and Silom Line (central). THB 17–59 per trip. Rabbit Card (contactless prepaid) is the equivalent of an Oyster card.
transport.mrt_subway: MRT covers Chatuchak, Silom, Lumphini. Connects with BTS at Asok/Sukhumvit interchange.
transport.grab: Always faster and cheaper than unbooked taxis. Essential app. Download before arrival.
transport.taxi: Metered. Always say 'meter, please' before getting in. Flag fall THB 35. If driver refuses meter, take the next taxi.
transport.chao_phraya: Chao Phraya Express Boat — orange flag (THB 15/stop, authentic), tourist boat (THB 40 unlimited). Khlong Saen Saep canal boat connects east and west Bangkok.
transport.tuk_tuk: Never accept a temple tour from a tuk-tuk driver — it is a shopping commission tour. Use only for agreed short-distance rides with price negotiated before boarding.
transport.airport_links: BKK Suvarnabhumi: Airport Rail Link to Phaya Thai BTS in 30 mins, THB 45. Grab: THB 250–350 to Sukhumvit.
transport.motorcycle_taxi: Orange-vest motorcycles at every BTS station. Fast for short distances. THB 10–60. Negotiate first.

trafficIntelligence.worstDay: Monday morning and Friday evening — absolute worst
trafficIntelligence.bestCrossCity: BTS Skytrain or MRT always faster during rush hours. NEVER plan taxi journeys across the city 7–9am or 5–8pm.
trafficIntelligence.rushHours: 7–9am and 5–8pm. Add 45–90 minutes to all taxi journey estimates.
trafficIntelligence.rainWarning: When it rains heavily in Bangkok, Grab surge goes 2–3x and taxis disappear. Take BTS before checking your phone.
trafficIntelligence.itineraryRule: Plan all temple visits before 10am. All market visits before noon. Afternoon: AC activities or rest. Late evening: street food and Yaowarat.
trafficIntelligence.friday: Friday evening 5–9pm is the worst traffic of the week. If departing Bangkok on a Friday evening, allow 2+ hours extra for airport.

novemberFebruary.reality: Best weather. Dry, cooler, ideal. Peak tourist season — book accommodation 4–6 weeks ahead. Loy Krathong in November (floating lanterns on river — extraordinary).

marchMay.reality: Hot season. Shoulder prices. Songkran (Thai New Year, April 13–15) — city-wide water fight. Extraordinary or overwhelming depending on preference.

junOct.reality: Rainy season. Heavy afternoon rain, mornings usually clear. 40–50% lower hotel prices. Bangkok in the rain is photogenic. Temples in the rain are extraordinary.

bangkokFestivals.loyKrathong: November full moon. Floating lanterns (krathong) on the Chao Phraya and canals. The river at night is covered in floating lights. Extraordinary visual experience. Free to participate.
bangkokFestivals.songkran: April 13–15. Thai New Year water festival. City-wide water fight — everyone gets wet. Sukhumvit is the epicentre. Unique and social but requires waterproofing all electronics.
bangkokFestivals.vegetarianFestival: October (9 days). Chinatown Yaowarat turns into a vegetarian food paradise. White-clothed devotees, incense, fire-walking ceremonies, extraordinary food.
bangkokFestivals.makha_bucha: February full moon. Buddhist holiday. Candlelit circumambulation ceremonies at major temples including Wat Pho. Free to observe respectfully.
bangkokFestivals.chakri_day: April 6. Thai national holiday commemorating the Chakri dynasty. Grand Palace area has ceremonies.

rooftopBars.name: Vertigo & Moon Bar — Banyan Tree
rooftopBars.note: Best 360° view. Open-air. Book dinner for best experience.

rooftopBars.name: Sky Bar — Lebua State Tower
rooftopBars.note: The famous Hangover Part II bar. THB 700/cocktail minimum. More famous than it is good but genuinely dramatic.

rooftopBars.name: Above Eleven
rooftopBars.note: Most accessible rooftop. No minimum. Peruvian-Japanese cocktails. Best value rooftop in Bangkok.

rooftopBars.name: Octave — Marriott Sukhumvit
rooftopBars.note: Three floors of rooftop. 360° views. More social than Vertigo, more affordable than Sky Bar.

rooftopBars.name: Chao Phraya riverbank at dusk (free)
rooftopBars.note: Free view of Wat Arun lit at dusk from the riverbank. The most beautiful free view in Bangkok.

ayutthaya.distance: 80km north, 1.5 hours by train or minibus
ayutthaya.note: Former Thai capital (1350–1767). UNESCO Heritage ruins of ancient temples, massive Buddha heads entwined in tree roots. Day trip from Bangkok by train: THB 15 from Hua Lamphong station. Full day required.
ayutthaya.bestTime: Early departure (7am train) to maximise time before afternoon heat

kanchanaburi.note: Bridge on the River Kwai. WWII history and Allied War Cemetery. River Kwai floating raft houses. The context is genuinely moving. Day trip or overnight.
kanchanaburi.transport: Direct bus from Southern Bus Terminal, THB 100

amphawa_floating_market.note: The authentic floating market for Thai day-trippers — not the tourist version at Damnoen Saduak. Evening firefly boat trips on the canals. Saturday–Sunday only.

pattaya.note: Beach city with complex reputation. The beach itself is mediocre. Worth visiting for: Koh Larn island (ferry from Pattaya pier, THB 30, excellent beach), Sanctuary of Truth (ornate wooden temple), and the Underwater World aquarium.

shopping.chatuchak: Weekend only. 8,000 stalls. Section 2–3 antiques and vintage. Section 25 home décor. Section 7 plants. The map is essential.
shopping.pratunam: The wholesale fashion district. The same factory-produced clothes sold in malls at THB 800 are available here at THB 150–200. No name brands but genuine quality. Platinum Fashion Mall and Pratunam Market.
shopping.mahaharat_market: Near Grand Palace. Amulets and Buddha images. The antique Thai Buddhist artefacts here are sold to monks and collectors — genuine items at genuine prices.
shopping.jj_market_vintage: Chatuchak section 2–3 has genuine vintage clothing, original 1970s–1990s pieces. The collectors who shop here arrive at 7am before the market officially opens.
shopping.gold_district: Yaowarat gold shops — similar to Dubai Gold Souk. 23K Thai gold. Check daily gold rate. The design tradition is different from Indian gold — more intricate filigree.
shopping.thai_silk: Jim Thompson (luxury, genuine Thai silk). Doi Tung (social enterprise, excellent quality). Never buy silk from tour-guide-recommended shops — commission is 50–100% of price.

critical: Remove shoes before entering temples and Thai homes — always, without exception.
Never touch a monk. Women must never hand anything directly to a monk — place it on a surface for the monk to pick up.
The head is sacred — never touch anyone's head including children.
Feet are the lowest — never point feet at a person, a Buddha image, or the altar.
Dress modestly for temples: shoulders covered, knees covered. Sarongs available at entrances THB 20–30 hire.
culturalRules.royalFamily: The Thai royal family is held in the deepest reverence. Any criticism of the monarchy is lèse-majesté — a criminal offence with imprisonment. This is enforced. Never make any comment about the royal family, positive or negative, in any public or social media context.
culturalRules.dressCode: Temple visits: shoulders and knees covered. Beach and street: casual. Nicer restaurants: smart casual.
culturalRules.bargaining: Expected in markets. Not in malls or restaurants. 30–40% reduction from opening price in tourist markets. Always smile throughout — a smile is the entire basis of negotiation.
culturalRules.tipping: Not customary but appreciated. THB 20–50 for good restaurant service. Not expected at street stalls.

visaIntelligence.indianPassport: Thai tourist visa required. Best: e-Visa at thaievisa.go.th (USD 35, 3–5 working days, 60 days single entry). Visa on Arrival available at airport (USD 35, 30 days) but queue 2+ hours. ALWAYS apply e-Visa.
visaIntelligence.important: Passport valid minimum 6 months. Return ticket and proof of accommodation required.
visaIntelligence.extension: Tourist visa extendable once at Thai Immigration Office for THB 1,900 for 30 more days.
visaIntelligence.visaRun: If extending stay: Aranyaprathet/Poipet border crossing (3 hours from Bangkok by train) for a same-day visa run. Common for long-term visitors.

savingsIntelligence: Exchange at Superrich Thailand (green kiosks in malls) vs airport — saves 8–12% on total exchange
BTS Skytrain vs taxi for any journey during rush hours — saves 45–90 minutes AND money
Or Tor Kor Market food vs equivalent restaurant food — saves 70% for same quality
Orange-flag Chao Phraya boat (THB 15) vs tourist boat (THB 40) — same river, same temples, THB 25 saved per journey
Wat Pho traditional massage school (THB 260/hour) vs tourist spa (THB 600–900/hour) — same or better quality
Chatuchak market weekend vintage vs same items in tourist shops Sukhumvit — saves 50–70% on vintage clothing
Street food breakfast at local vendor (THB 60–80) vs hotel breakfast (THB 300–600) — saves THB 240–520/person/day
Grab app vs street taxi — saves 20–30% and eliminates meter refusal stress
e-Visa (60-day) vs Visa on Arrival (30-day) — same cost, double the time, no airport queue

practical.electricity: Type A and B (American-style). 220V. Indian plugs need adapter. Available at 7-Eleven THB 80–150.
practical.bestExchange: Superrich Thailand (green kiosks) or Vasu exchange — rates 8–12% better than airport. Never at airport.
practical.simCard: True Move H and DTAC at airport arrivals: THB 300–500 for 30GB/7 days. Best tourist option.
practical.tipping: Restaurants: THB 20–50 if no service charge. Taxis: round up. Street food: never expected.
practical.apps: Grab (rides), BTS SkytTrain app, Klook (activities and booking), Wongnai (Thai restaurant discovery in Thai — shows local places Google doesn't), Line (messaging app everyone in Thailand uses)

hiddenPlaces.name: Bang Krachao
hiddenPlaces.note: Green lung of Bangkok. Ferry THB 4 + bicycle THB 50. No cars. Mangrove forest. The Bangkok of 1970.

hiddenPlaces.name: Talad Noi
hiddenPlaces.note: Oldest Chinese neighbourhood. Portuguese shophouses. Cats on motorcycles. Art students' coffee shops. Undiscovered.

hiddenPlaces.name: Or Tor Kor Market
hiddenPlaces.note: Where Bangkok chefs shop. Prepared food section is city's best-kept food secret. Air-conditioned.

hiddenPlaces.name: Nang Loeng Market
hiddenPlaces.note: Bangkok's oldest market (1899). Art Deco shophouses. Traditional Thai desserts made by 3-generation families. Almost no tourists.

hiddenPlaces.name: Khlong Lat Mayom floating market
hiddenPlaces.note: Sat–Sun. The floating market Bangkok residents actually go to — not the tourist version.

hiddenPlaces.name: Ari neighbourhood
hiddenPlaces.note: BTS Ari. Design and creative quarter. Independent coffee roasters, vinyl shops, art galleries. Zero tourists.

hiddenPlaces.name: Wat Ratchanatdaram (Loha Prasat)
hiddenPlaces.note: The Metal Castle — a 37-spire metal tower adjacent to the Democracy Monument. Free entry. Almost never mentioned in guides.

hiddenPlaces.name: Talad Rot Fai (Train Market) Ratchada
hiddenPlaces.note: Thursday–Sunday evenings. Best vintage market in Bangkok. Green neon, food stalls, collectors. Excellent photography.

hiddenPlaces.name: Pridi Phanomyong Museum
hiddenPlaces.note: The preserved home of the founder of Thai democracy. Free entry. The most politically significant house in Thailand. Almost no tourists.

insiderIntelligence: 7-Eleven in Bangkok is not a convenience store — it is a legitimate food destination. The Milo dinosaur (cold Milo with undissolved powder on top) is specifically Thai and costs THB 20.

The cheapest and best Thai massage in Bangkok is at Wat Pho's traditional massage school (THB 260/hour). You are massaged by students supervised by masters — the quality equals tourist spas at 20% of the price.
Thai fruit in season (mango April–June, durian June–August) is meaningfully better than Thai fruit out of season. Or Tor Kor has the finest seasonal fruit in the city.
Bangkok's food is hottest at lunch, milder at breakfast. Order your spice level: 'ped nit noi' = mildly spicy, 'ped mak' = very spicy.
The Skytrain map shows stations as evenly spaced — they are not. Some station-to-station walks are 5 minutes, some are 20. Check Google Maps before deciding to walk.
Bangkok has more Michelin-starred street food stalls than any city other than Hong Kong. The Michelin Guide Thailand lists vendors at THB 50–100/dish alongside restaurants at THB 3,000/person.
The royal family image is displayed in almost every business in Thailand. It is treated with deep reverence — the national anthem plays in cinemas before every film and everyone stands.
Thai Buddhist monks cannot accept anything from a woman's hand directly. If you are a woman and want to give an offering to a monk, place it on a cloth or table surface for the monk to pick up.
The Grand Palace closes at 3:30pm. Temple entry closes at 3pm. Arriving at 2pm guarantees a rushed experience. Morning is always the correct time.

Bangkok's red-light districts (Patpong, Nana, Soi Cowboy) are tourist attractions in the sense that many visitors walk through them. They are genuinely part of the city's social landscape and not dangerous to observe.
whyPeopleFallInLove: People arrive for the temples. They stay for the food — specifically for the moment they eat something extraordinary from a stall with no English menu and no Instagram presence, standing on the street at 11pm, and realise the finest meal of their trip cost THB 80. They return for the neighbourhoods — Talad Noi at 8am, Bang Krachao by bicycle on a Sunday, the canal at sunset when the light turns everything amber. Bangkok rewards the person who stops trying to see it and starts letting it happen.
localTruths: Most visitors think Bangkok is traffic. Locals think Bangkok is food — the Or Tor Kor market at dawn, the Jay Fai wok at midnight, the 7-Eleven that is genuinely a meal destination. The traffic is the price. The food is the reason.

Most visitors think Bangkok is temples. Young Thais think Bangkok is rooftops, vinyl records in Shimokitazawa-equivalent Ari, the craft beer scene in Thonglor. Two completely different cities occupy the same geography.

Most visitors think Bangkok is chaotic. Bangkok runs on a precise social order that takes 3 days to begin to read. The apparent chaos is organised. The apparent rudeness is formality. The apparent smile is genuine.

ifYouOnlyHadOneChance.breakfast: Or Tor Kor Market at 8am — Bangkok's professional chefs shop here. The mango sticky rice uses mangoes at peak ripeness because vendors compete with each other daily. The prepared food section contains dishes that don't appear on any restaurant menu.
ifYouOnlyHadOneChance.sunset: Chao Phraya River on the orange-flag express boat at 5pm — THB 15, workers going home, temples lit against the sky, the city from the water at golden hour. The cheapest and most honest view of Bangkok available.
ifYouOnlyHadOneChance.neighbourhood: Talad Noi at 9am — the oldest Chinese neighbourhood, Portuguese shophouses from the 1800s, cats on motorcycles, coffee shops in converted warehouses run by art students. The neighbourhood that hasn't been discovered yet.
ifYouOnlyHadOneChance.meal: Jay Fai at opening — a 70-year-old woman in ski goggles against the wok flames, Michelin-starred since 2018, the crab omelette the most argued-about dish in Bangkok. The queue is two hours. The two hours are correct.
ifYouOnlyHadOneChance.memory: Wat Pho at 6am — the monks chanting morning sutras, the incense smoke rising straight in the still air, the 46-metre reclining Buddha lit by the first light through the temple windows. The working temple before it becomes a tourist attraction.
ifYouOnlyHadOneChance.secret: Bang Krachao by bicycle on a Sunday morning — ferry THB 4 from Klong Toei pier, bicycle hire THB 50, mangrove forest, wooden houses on stilts, the air noticeably different from the city fifteen minutes away. The Bangkok of 1970 that somehow still exists.

residentSunday: A Bangkok resident with one free Sunday: 7am Or Tor Kor Market — the mango sticky rice, the prepared food section, the freshest produce in Bangkok. 9am drive or taxi to Bang Krachao — ferry THB 4, bicycle hire THB 50, mangrove forest, wooden houses, the air genuinely different. Back by noon. 1pm lunch at a neighbourhood restaurant in Thonglor that no tourist has found. 3pm afternoon nap — this is accepted and correct. 6pm Chatuchak area if the weekend market is still open, or a neighbourhood café in Ari. 8pm Yaowarat for one dish. This is the Bangkok that residents describe when asked what they actually do on weekends.

dayMemoryTargets.arrival: The first moment the scale of Bangkok becomes real — the elevated highway at night, the neon below, the density, the smells through the taxi window. Then the first extraordinary food from a stall with no English menu that costs THB 60 and is better than anything back home. The memory is the gap between what the traveller expected Bangkok to be and what it actually is.
dayMemoryTargets.peak: The Jay Fai moment — standing in the queue for two hours, watching a 70-year-old woman in ski goggles work a wok flame, finally eating the crab omelette that required the two hours. OR the Bang Krachao moment — bicycle in the mangrove forest, air noticeably different, a city of 14 million people fifteen minutes away and completely absent. The memory is the moment Bangkok revealed its other self.
dayMemoryTargets.departure: The last bowl of something from a stall that the traveller found themselves, not from a list. The Skytrain at rush hour one final time. The specific quality of Bangkok heat at 9am when the city is already fully operational. The memory is the realisation that they understand this city slightly — and the desire to come back and understand it more.

two_days.note: Two days in Bangkok should be three experiences done deeply. The temple, the river, the street food. Bangkok rewards depth over breadth more than almost any other city.

skip: Day trips to Ayutthaya or Kanchanaburi
three_to_four_days.note: Three to four days is the ideal first Bangkok trip. Enough to discover what the city actually is.

five_to_six_days.note: Now day trips are viable and the neighbourhood character of Bangkok can be properly experienced.

seven_plus_days.note: At 7+ days the traveller can move between Bangkok's layers — tourist, expat, local — and begin to understand how they relate to each other.

antiPatterns: Grand Palace AND Wat Pho on the same morning — both require 2+ hours and significant walking in heat. One per morning only.
Chatuchak Market AND Yaowarat in the same day — Chatuchak is 3-4 hours in morning heat, Yaowarat peaks at 9pm. The gap requires a full afternoon rest that most people don't plan for.
Floating market AND Ayutthaya as a combined day trip — they are in opposite directions from Bangkok. Combined, neither gets sufficient time.
Muay Thai evening AND an early morning temple visit the next day — Muay Thai ends at 10pm minimum. A 7am temple visit the next morning produces an exhausted person at both.
Cooking class AND Chatuchak on the same day — the cooking class market visit starts at 8am and the class runs until 1pm. Chatuchak needs to be a separate day.

combinationIntelligence.emotionalArc: Spiritual → moving through the city → sensory peak. Bangkok's three defining registers in correct sequence.
The market that feeds the city → the nature that sustains it → the street where it celebrates.
Physical intensity → warm recovery. Effort followed by reward.

photographyIntelligence.droneRules: CAT permit required for commercial drone use. Tourist recreational drones: technically require permission. Enforcement inconsistent but drones near royal/government buildings strictly prohibited.

accessibility.wheelchairFriendly: Improving — newer areas good, old city challenging
accessibility.metroAccessibility: BTS Skytrain has lifts at major stations. MRT fully accessible.
accessibility.challengingAreas: Old City temples have steps, Khao San area uneven surfaces
accessibility.note: Wheelchair accessible tuk-tuks available through specific operators
